heading: Public only when used
body:
A public member promises that other code calls it. When nothing calls it, a reader must search the whole project to learn that it is only a helper. So Tachyon keeps a member public only when something outside the class uses it.

The build refuses, with `TY1333`, a public method or field of a class in `services`, `helpers`, `controllers` or `utils` when nothing outside the class uses it. A member stays public when:

- **the view uses it:** a Tac view reads or calls `cart.total()` for `CartService`. Case and `_` do not matter, so `cart.itemCount` also matches `ItemCount` in C# and Go and `item_count` in Ruby, Python and Rust;
- **another class uses it:** a class of the same realm needs the class and calls the member, such as `this.priceService.total()` or `PriceUtils.label(total)`;
- **Tachyon uses it:** the member or one of its parameters has an annotation (`OnEvent`, `GetRoute`, `OnStart`, `Cached`, `Check` and the others); it is a field that Tachyon fills (a field without a starting value, or a field that `Needs` or `NeedsAll` fills); a setup hands the class to Tachyon; a `Gateway` names the class file, such as `{"class":"server/services/ReportService.java"}`; it is `identify` of the `IdentityProvider`; or it is a name that the runtime or the language calls, such as `hotState`, `toString` or Go `String`.

A call from a test does not keep a member public. Test the member through the public member that uses it. Models, entities, errors and test files are not checked. A private member that nothing calls is dead code: delete it, because the coverage check refuses it too.

Make a member private in the form of your language:

| Language | Private form |
| --- | --- |
| TypeScript, Java, Groovy, Kotlin, Swift, PHP | `private total()` |
| C# | `private int Total()`, or no access modifier: `int Total()`. `public` and `internal` members are public |
| JavaScript | `_total()`, a name that starts with `_` |
| Dart, Python | `_total`, a name that starts with `_` |
| Ruby | `private def total`, or the method below a `private` line |
| Go | `total`, a name that starts with a lowercase letter |
| Rust | `fn total(&self)`, without `pub` |

`ty migrate fix --write` makes the simple cases private for you: it writes `private`, removes `pub`, or renames the member and its uses in the class. It leaves a member alone when the new name is taken or a use is not clear.

The check is on by default, like the other design rules. While you migrate, you can turn it off for one side of the app: for Tac code, set `tac.visibility.check` to `false` in `client/manifest.json`; for Yon code, set `visibility.check` to `false` in `server/application.json`. `ty migrate check` lists every place to change, even when the setting is off.
